## Dataset

Each row represents **one country in one report year**. The file contains **1,969 rows** in a single sheet — `Data for Figure 2.1 (2011–2024)` — spanning **13 report years** (2011, 2012, and 2014–2024; **2013 is not included**), with **137–158 countries per year** and **168 unique countries overall**. This file has **one consistent schema across all years**, so no harmonisation step is needed before cross-year analysis.

### Per-year structure

| Year | Rows (countries) |
|------|------------------|
| 2011 | 156              |
| 2012 | 156              |
| 2014 | 158              |
| 2015 | 157              |
| 2016 | 155              |
| 2017 | 156              |
| 2018 | 156              |
| 2019 | 153              |
| 2020 | 149              |
| 2021 | 146              |
| 2022 | 137              |
| 2023 | 143              |
| 2024 | 147              |

All years share the **same 13 columns**. Row counts vary only because the set of surveyed countries changes slightly each year.

### Key variables

| Concept | Column name | What it measures |
|------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| **Year** | `Year` | Report year (2011–2024, no 2013) |
| **Country** | `Country name` | The nation — the unit of analysis |
| **Rank** | `Rank` | Position in that year's global ranking |
| **Happiness score ★** | `Life evaluation (3-year average)` | Cantril-ladder life evaluation, 0–10, averaged over 3 years — the **TARGET** variable |
| **Lower whisker** | `Lower whisker` | Lower bound of the 95% confidence whisker around the score |
| **Upper whisker** | `Upper whisker` | Upper bound of the 95% confidence whisker |
| **GDP per capita** | `Explained by: Log GDP per capita` | Contribution of income (log GDP) to the score |
| **Social support** | `Explained by: Social support` | Contribution of having someone to count on |
| **Life expectancy** | `Explained by: Healthy life expectancy` | Contribution of healthy longevity |
| **Freedom** | `Explained by: Freedom to make life choices` | Contribution of freedom over life choices |
| **Generosity** | `Explained by: Generosity` | Contribution of charitable behaviour |
| **Corruption** | `Explained by: Perceptions of corruption` | Contribution of perceived honesty / low corruption |
| **Dystopia residual** | `Dystopia + residual` | Unexplained remainder above the Dystopia baseline |

★ = target variable.

**Note:** There is **no `Region` column** in this file. If you want regional groupings (e.g. Western Europe, Sub-Saharan Africa), you'll need to join in a country → region mapping yourself.

### A subtlety that shapes the whole analysis

**The six "Explained by:" columns are not raw measurements.**

- **What they actually are:** each `Explained by: …` column is the *estimated contribution* of that factor to the country's life-evaluation score — **not** the raw value (it is **not** GDP in dollars, not years of life expectancy, etc.).
- **They are additive:** the six contributions plus `Dystopia + residual` sum (up to rounding) to `Life evaluation (3-year average)`. The bars in the report literally stack to the total.
- **Why it matters:** a model that "predicts" the score from these seven columns will score near-perfectly almost by construction. For genuine modelling, treat these as decomposition outputs and bring in **external raw features** (real GDP, life-expectancy years, corruption indices, etc.) instead.
